title: Chemical splash in the eye
summary: Any chemical in the eye is an emergency. Continuous flushing with clean water in the first minutes makes the biggest difference to saving the eye.
steps: Start rinsing the eye with clean cool water immediately. Every second counts.
Hold the eyelids open. Tilt the head so water runs from the inner corner outward and away from the other eye.
Rinse continuously for at least 20 minutes — use a slow-running tap, jug, or clean container refilled as needed.
If contact lenses are in, try to remove them while rinsing — but do not delay rinsing to do so.
Keep the person calm. Cover both eyes loosely with a clean cloth after rinsing — moving one eye moves the other.
Arrange immediate transport to an emergency department. Take the chemical container or label with you if safe to do so.
avoid: Do not try to neutralise the chemical with another substance.
Do not apply eye drops, oils, or home remedies.
Do not stop rinsing early — keep going right up to medical help arriving.
whenToEscalate: Always — every chemical splash in the eye is an emergency, even if the eye feels better after rinsing.
Immediately for strong alkalis (drain cleaner, oven cleaner, cement dust, lime) — these damage faster than acids.
If vision is blurred or lost, the eye is bleeding, or the eyelid is severely swollen.
specialty: Emergency department or eye casualty unit immediately.
